I have had good experiences and bad experiences. Every bad experience I have had was because I ate too many. Now when I do it I stay around 2 grams. Every trip is very different for me. Sometimes I have vivid hallucinations, like clouds or distant hills morphing into shapes. Once I climbed a tree and almost cried thinking about how unique it was compared to other trees. Once I looked at the time on my phone and it looked like alien letters, it meant absolutely nothing to me. However, the most "spiritual" experience I have had was after eating about 6 grams. It was about 5 years ago so I'll recreate it to the best of my ability. I was camping with some friends, 4 or 5 total. A buddy and I both decided we were going to trip some balls on that camp out. The camp we set up was in a secluded forest area by a river. We waited until it was dark, and ingested our mushrooms. I started feeling elated on the come up and decided to go hiking on a trail with a more sober friend so he could smoke some weed. As we sat there I looked down into the dirt and it began to look like Aztec symbols. Like everywhere I looked on the ground had symbols etched into it. Then as we were walking back on a very distinct trail, I became very confused about directions. I would turn 90 degrees and it looked like the trail stretched off into the distance, turn 90 degrees and same thing. The trail was about 4 feet wide and very distinct, like a dirt road almost. Luckily my friend was there to guide me back or I would have walked off into the woods thinking I was following a trail of Aztec symbols. When we got back, shit really hit the fan, so I crawled into a tent occupied with a few of my fellow campers and listened to them talk and laugh to calm down. At this point everywhere I looked was glowing neon orange and had arrows racing over it in a direction, like arrows flowing on some set course over all lines on the tent walls. As I bugged out on this, I started hunching down lower and lower, and felt as though I was shrinking! I shrank and shrank until the tent was gargantuan, as if I were only 6 inches tall. That was too much, and I was starting to trip harder. I closed my eyes and started imagining. As I lay there with my eyes closed, the sound of the rushing river overwhelmed my senses and that was all I could hear. All I could see was darkness (eyes closed). I started wondering what had happened to me, like I couldn't remember I was on drugs. I concluded I had died, fallen into the river that was overwhelming me and died. I thought about the afterlife, and concluded that going into the afterlife was as simple as switching a light on. It is hard to explain, but I envisioned that it was a choice to believe in an afterlife or not at that moment, switching the light on meant afterlife, leaving it off meant eternal darkness. I also had this vivid vision of the sun rising over a hill and setting, and a tombstone rising up on this hill. It was my life flashing by, it was time. Time became meaningless to me, laying there in the dark with the river. I accepted my death and wanted the light. I woke up out of this immobile state what must have been a couple hours later because everybody was asleep. I never ate more than 2 grams of shrooms after that, and have only done it a few times since.

Psilocybin is personally one of my favorite drugs because it allows you to enter an altered mental state that can offer some very powerful insights on your personal state of being, your life, and the universe that surrounds you. I know that sounds like a bunch of hippy dippy baloney, but for what it's worth, I have always been a very empirically-minded, materialist person and was initially very skeptical of people's claims regarding psilocybin until I tried it myself out of curiosity. It is almost cliche to talk about "expanding one's consciousness," but there is definitely something to the psychedelic experience that is genuinely unlike anything else.

If you are a curious and open minded person and you generally have your shit together when it comes to the basics of life and mental fortitude, I highly recommend it. Just remember that, while a psilocybin trip can be very euphoric, it can also force you to confront things that you may be uncomfortable with, things that may challenge your sense of self and view of the universe at a very fundamental level. Personally, I like such "challenges" but if you are not comfortable exploring the unfamiliar or even the disturbing, shrooms might not be for you. Good luck.
